# NL2SQL is a solved problem... Not!

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#nl2sql-not-solved)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-13**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/cidrdb/papers/2024/p74-floratou.pdf) · CIDR 2024 proceedings PDF; eight pages

**Reading coverage:** All eight pages: Sections 1–6, definitions, experiments, metric rules, limitations and references. Figures 1–4 and their captions were inspected in rendered pages 2, 4, 6 and 7. The PDF contains no appendix. The linked public tool was inspected separately without execution.

**Additional inspected sources:** [CIDR proceedings record](https://vldb.org/cidrdb/2024/nl2sql-is-a-solved-problem-not.html) · [Archerfish comparator at inspected revision](https://github.com/archerfish-bench/benchmark/blob/620fbcc4cff11dfbc8d17db20fc762073b43afa3/src/benchmark/utils/result_set_match.py) · [Archerfish README at inspected revision](https://github.com/archerfish-bench/benchmark/blob/620fbcc4cff11dfbc8d17db20fc762073b43afa3/README.md)

## Research question

Single-reference evaluation can reject plausible interpretations of an underspecified question, while a system may generate SQL even when the database cannot supply the requested information.

## Method

Defines ambiguity through multiple acceptable, non-equivalent SQL interpretations. Probes ambiguity with two annotators and prompted GPT-3.5/GPT-4, and probes semantic mismatch by pairing questions with an unrelated database. Proposes relaxed execution matching based on row order, extra output columns and alternative candidate keys, implemented through the Archerfish framework.

## Evaluation

The ambiguity study covers 272 KaggleDBQA questions and marks a question ambiguous when either annotator does. The mismatch experiment sends Spider questions to the KaggleDBQA crime database with two prompt examples. Metric comparisons use GPT-4 on three Spider databases; additional preliminary studies concern schema selection, demographic-column detection and multilingual/dialect behavior.

## What the results support

The union of two annotators flags 112 questions; Figure 2 reports 62.1% human agreement and 65.8% GPT-4/human agreement. These are agreement rates, not correctness scores. Relaxed matching accepts more outputs than execution matching on the three illustrated databases, showing sensitivity to evaluator rules. The mismatch result concerns a deliberately unrelated-schema setup.

## Limits and qualifications

A position paper with small or selectively reported studies, historical models and informal customer input rather than a controlled intent-satisfaction study. A higher score under a more permissive metric does not demonstrate better SQL generation. The metric remains tied to one database instance and selected relaxation rules. The public article also discusses nonpublic safety experiments; those results were not independently accessible or reproduced.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides historical evidence and definitions directly relevant to ambiguity, answerability and evaluator design, together with an inspectable example of how intent-oriented relaxations change accepted answers.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
